title: Floats
summary: Float moves an element to one side and lets text flow around it.

subtopics.title: Main property
subtopics.explanation: `float: left` moves an element to the left side of its containing area. Text and inline content can flow around it. It is like placing a photo beside a magazine paragraph. Use it for this text-wrapping effect, not as a general alignment system. For example, a floated image in an article can have text wrap beside it.

subtopics.title: What it changes
subtopics.explanation: Content can wrap beside a floated item until it reaches the item’s height or a clearing boundary. This can make later sections unexpectedly move alongside the float. It is like text wrapping around an image on a printed page. Inspect the whole surrounding layout when adding floats. For example, a following heading may need clear when it must begin beneath that image.

subtopics.title: Another useful choice
subtopics.explanation: `clear` tells an element to move below floats on one or both sides. It is like starting a new paragraph after the picture ends. Older layouts often used clearing techniques to contain floats; modern layout systems usually provide simpler ways to arrange components. For example, if the parent collapses around floats, use a modern containment approach or layout system.

subtopics.title: Common behavior
subtopics.explanation: Floated children may not contribute to a parent’s height in the way beginners expect. This can make the parent appear empty and allow later content to overlap. It is like stacking a picture outside the box used to measure the page. Understand the containing layout before mixing floats with other rules. For example, do not use floats to align a navigation bar or card grid.

subtopics.title: Good practice
subtopics.explanation: Use Flexbox or Grid for navigation, cards, and component layouts. They provide direct alignment and spacing controls. Floats are a specialized text-wrapping tool, like placing an illustration beside an article. Choosing the right layout model makes responsive behavior easier to reason about. For example, check the text wrap at narrow width so the line measure remains readable.

foundations.overview: A float moves an element to one side so nearby text can flow around it. Floats were designed for wrapping text around images, such as in an article. Think of a picture placed beside a paragraph in a magazine. They are usually the wrong tool for arranging modern app layouts; use Flexbox or Grid for rows, columns, and alignment.
foundations.whyItMatters: Floats remain useful for text wrapping, but they are a specialized layout tool. Using them for general component arrangement creates harder-to-maintain behavior.
foundations.browserPerspective: When laying out, the browser takes the floated box out of normal flow, positions it against the chosen edge of its containing block, and then lays out subsequent line boxes shortened to avoid the float. Floats are contained by Block Formatting Contexts, which is why overflow/flow-root parents wrap them.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Wrapping article text around an image or pull quote, drop-cap-style first letters, small inline figures in blog posts, and maintaining or migrating older float-based layouts.
foundations.businessImpact: Editorial and content sites still rely on float-based text wrapping for readable, magazine-style articles; understanding it keeps content rendering correctly.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Recognizing float pitfalls (collapsed parents, clearing) speeds up debugging legacy layouts and informs safe migrations to Flexbox or Grid.
foundations.performanceImpact: Floats are cheap to lay out, but float-based page layouts often require extra wrapper elements and clearfix, increasing DOM size and CSS complexity compared with Flexbox/Grid.
commonUseCases: Wrapping paragraph text around an image or figure
Floating a pull quote or sidebar callout within an article
Reading and maintaining legacy float-based grid layouts
Clearing floats so a parent wraps its floated children

commonMisconceptions.myth: Floats are the right way to build page layouts.
commonMisconceptions.reality: That was a pre-Flexbox/Grid workaround; today use Flexbox for components and Grid for page layout, and floats for text wrapping.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A parent automatically grows to contain its floated children.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Floats are out of flow, so the parent collapses; you must clear them (clearfix or display: flow-root).

commonMisconceptions.myth: clear and float do the same thing.
commonMisconceptions.reality: float positions an element and lets content wrap; clear forces an element below preceding floats.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Float is the modern default for building columns.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Grid and Flexbox provide clearer controls for multi-column component layouts.
Clear affects float wrapping; it does not replace sizing and layout debugging.

visualExplorer.title: How floats wrap text and collapse parents
visualExplorer.caption: Step through floating an image, wrapping text, the collapsed-parent problem, and the clearfix fix.

steps.title: Normal flow
steps.description: An image sits on its own line and text follows below it in normal document flow.

steps.title: float: left
steps.description: The image shifts to the left edge and leaves normal flow; the paragraph text wraps around its right side.

steps.title: Collapsed parent
steps.description: If the parent contains only floats, it collapses to zero height and its background/border disappear.

steps.title: clear
steps.description: An element with clear: both moves below the float instead of wrapping beside it.

steps.title: Clearfix / flow-root
steps.description: A clearfix pseudo-element or display: flow-root makes the parent contain its floats again.

interactiveExamples.title: Wrap text around a floated image
interactiveExamples.explanation: float: left pulls the box to the left and the paragraph flows around it.

files.index.html:
IMG

This paragraph wraps around the floated box on its left side, just like text flows around an image in a magazine article. As the text continues, it fills the space beside the float and then continues below it once it clears the height.
files.styles.css:
body { font-family: system-ui; padding: 20px; }
.figure { float: left; width: 90px; height: 90px; background: #3b82f6; color: #fff; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 8px; margin: 0 16px 8px 0; }

interactiveExamples.expectedOutput: A blue box on the left with the paragraph text wrapping around its right side and below it.

interactiveExamples.title: Fix a collapsed parent with clearfix
interactiveExamples.explanation: A parent of only floated children collapses; the clearfix pseudo-element makes it contain them again.
interactiveExamples.expectedOutput: The bordered row grows to wrap both floated columns instead of collapsing to a thin line.

codeLab.title: Make the parent contain its floats
codeLab.instructions: The .gallery wraps three floated thumbnails but collapses to no height. Make it contain them. Hint: add a clearfix pseudo-element (or use display: flow-root) on .gallery.
codeLab.expectedOutput: The bordered gallery wraps around all three thumbnails instead of collapsing.
hints: display: flow-root establishes a Block Formatting Context that contains floats with no extra markup.
The older approach is a clearfix: .gallery::after { content: ''; display: block; clear: both; }

keyTakeaways: `float: left` moves an element to the left side of its containing area.
Content can wrap beside a floated item until it reaches the item’s height or a clearing boundary.
`clear` tells an element to move below floats on one or both sides.
Floated children may not contribute to a parent’s height in the way beginners expect.
Use Flexbox or Grid for navigation, cards, and component layouts.
